items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: you are just like San Tomas, that you have to see to believe

ctx.x: What happened at the airport there? I understand something happened there that prompted you to write a tune.

Well, he asked me if the Puerto Ricans and the Americans danced very good the guaguanco, el cha cha cha, mambo, all the music from Cuba, and I said yes. And said: "oh, come on Machito, maybe you lose the touch because you've been in the United States for so long that now you consider anybody you see turning, that he is dancing Cuban music." I said, no, no, no, no, really, you are just like San Tomas, that you have to see to believe. So, I say goodbye to the guy and I get my plane. You know the pressure, the…
Okay. Now, you recorded that tune for "The Sun Also Rises" album, on the Tico label. What did you call that tune?
